title: Maybe the Pill Is Just the User Interface
topic: Open-label placebo and whether expectancy and ritual can be delivered digitally instead of mailing inert pills.

scene.environment: A surreal but photoreal pill candy land built as a physical set: oversized capsules and tablets, blister-pack paths, translucent gummy-colored pills, pill bottles as landscape towers. Satoshi is seated naturally in the environment beside an oversized capsule and a smartphone.
scene.wardrobe: rumpled dark overshirt over charcoal T-shirt; no suit or tie
scene.framing: waist-up, seated, natural adult proportions, face clearly visible

publications.title: Open-label placebo treatment in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial
publications.finding: Open-label placebo plus treatment as usual reduced pain and disability more than treatment as usual alone.

beats.text: A placebo pill may be less like a drug than a user interface.
Carvalho randomized chronic low-back-pain patients to open-label placebo, and pain and disability still improved.
Apparently Santa can still bring presents even after you are told exactly how the sleigh works.
So if expectancy, ritual and repetition matter, mailing inert pills starts to look like a very expensive interface layer.

visual.screen_text: WHY ARE WE PAYING POSTAGE\nFOR THE INTERFACE?

beats.text: Maybe the pill is just the user interface, and the therapeutic machinery can live on the phone.
